nodes.6.1: RESOLVED: Kant employs duty-based deontological ethics: actions judged by conformity to universal moral rules, not consequences.
nodes.6.2: RESOLVED: Mill employs consequence-based utilitarian ethics: actions judged by whether they maximize overall happiness and minimize suffering.
nodes.6.3: RESOLVED: Key structural difference: Kant evaluates the nature of the act itself; Mill evaluates the results of the act.

nodes.6.1.1: RESOLVED: Kantian categorical imperative: Act only according to maxims that could be universal laws without contradiction.
nodes.6.1.2: RESOLVED: Kant prohibits lying categorically because universalizing 'lie when convenient' destroys the institution of truth-telling itself.
nodes.6.1.3: RESOLVED: For Kant, moral worth derives from acting from duty according to rational principle, not from achieving desired outcomes.
nodes.6.2.1: RESOLVED: Utilitarian calculus: weigh total pleasure/happiness against total pain/suffering produced by an action.
nodes.6.2.2: RESOLVED: Mill permits lying when specific lie prevents greater suffering than it causes, because net utility increases.
nodes.6.2.3: RESOLVED: Mill generally opposes lying because it typically causes more harm than good (erosion of trust, social instability), not because lying is intrinsically wrong.
nodes.6.3.1: DOCUMENT: Refugee hypothetical illustrates divergence: Authorities ask if you're harboring refugees.
nodes.6.3.2: RESOLVED: Kantian response: Tell truth because you cannot universalize 'lie to save lives' without destroying truth-telling as institution.
nodes.6.3.3: RESOLVED: Utilitarian response: Lie because suffering prevented (refugees killed) vastly exceeds harm of one lie.
nodes.6.4.1: QUESTION: Can rule-utilitarianism bridge the gap by adopting generally utility-maximizing rules that resemble Kantian duties?
nodes.6.4.2: QUESTION: Does Kantian prohibition on lying hold even when consequences are catastrophic, or does 'perfect duty' admit of no exceptions?
nodes.6.4.3: ASSUMES: Moral philosophy framework may be relevant to evaluating fiduciary conduct: whether trustees judged by adherence to fiduciary duty rules (Kantian) or by outcomes produced for beneficiaries (utilitarian).
